record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Can one prove a singularity theorem using the dominant energy condition rather than the timelike convergence condition?

evidence.quote: Prove a singularity theorem assuming the dominant energy condition rather than the timelike convergence condition. The DE condition is the most natural energy condition from a physical standpoint [HE], but unfortunately TCC seems to be the most useful from the standpoint of proving singularity theorems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian 4-manifold satisfying the Einstein field equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) - \tfrac{1}{2}R\, g = T$, where $T$ is the stress-energy tensor. Recall the following energy conditions:

(i) The timelike convergence condition (TCC): $\mathrm{Ric}(g)(X,X) \geq 0$ for every timelike vector $X$ (equivalent, via Einstein's equations, to the strong energy condition $T(X,X) \geq \tfrac{1}{2}(\mathrm{tr}_g T)\, g(X,X)$ for timelike $X$).

(ii) The dominant energy condition (DEC): for every future-directed causal vector $X$, the vector $-T(X,\cdot)^\sharp$ (with one index raised) is future-directed causal; equivalently, in any orthonormal frame, $T_{00} \geq |T_{ab}|$ for all $a,b$.

The classical Penrose–Hawking singularity theorems (e.g., Hawking's theorem deducing timelike geodesic incompleteness from the existence of a compact Cauchy hypersurface with everywhere-positive mean curvature, and analogous statements with trapped surfaces) all assume the timelike convergence condition. Physically the dominant energy condition is regarded as the most natural and robust energy condition, but it does not in general imply TCC.

Problem. Prove a singularity theorem (i.e., a theorem asserting causal or timelike geodesic incompleteness from suitable initial/causal data such as the existence of a trapped surface, a compact Cauchy hypersurface, or a point with reconverging light cone) under the assumption of the dominant energy condition in place of the timelike convergence condition, or else demonstrate that no such theorem can hold by exhibiting geodesically complete counterexamples satisfying DEC together with the relevant causal hypotheses.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that classical singularity theorems continue to rely on the strong/timelike convergence condition, with recent work (e.g., singularity theorems for Einstein–Klein–Gordon and Hawking-type theorems under worldvolume/quantum energy inequalities) replacing TCC with energy inequalities or specific matter models rather than with the bare dominant energy condition. No general singularity theorem assuming only the dominant energy condition appears in the literature, so the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Energy conditions in general relativity and quantum field theory
status_evidence.snippet: Hawking's singularity theorem concerns matter obeying the strong energy condition (SEC)... guaranteeing the timelike convergence property.
status_evidence.claim: Classical singularity theorems use the strong/timelike convergence condition, not DEC.

status_evidence.title: Hawking-type singularity theorems for worldvolume energy inequalities
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work replaces pointwise SEC/TCC with averaged or worldvolume energy inequalities to prove singularity theorems.
status_evidence.claim: Recent attempts weaken TCC via energy inequalities, but not via DEC alone.

status_evidence.title: A singularity theorem for Einstein–Klein–Gordon theory
status_evidence.snippet: Singularity theorem for specific matter models where SEC can be violated.
status_evidence.claim: Workarounds exist only for specific matter models, not a general DEC-based theorem.
